text:
Bitcoin pushed its recovery higher during Friday's midday session, testing resistance near $64,400 as the broader digital asset market cap climbed to $2.17 trillion (+1.9%). The rally consolidated gains following a $79.5 million short liquidation event and a three-day, $510 million spot ETF inflow reversal. Despite the technical breakout, the Fear & Greed Index remains pinned at 23 ("Extreme Fear"), reflecting underlying institutional caution ahead of next week's June CPI print.

Macro markets experienced a selective capital rotation as stock futures pulled back to absorb Nasdaq's oversubscribed SK Hynix listing — the largest foreign IPO in U.S. history. Treasury yields remained supportive, with the 10-year yield easing to 4.53% following solid demand at the recent 30-year bond auction. Stable yields and a cooling U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) continue to relieve the mechanical opportunity cost pressure on Bitcoin, supporting its near-term base.
